title: Define graceful-degradation bands and rollback criteria for Hosted Chat SLOs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define a concrete SLO matrix, graded degradation bands, and automated rollout/rollback gates for the Hosted Chat product line so that we can ship upcoming runtime-1.20 optimizations without exposing customers to silent regressions. This ticket covers target latency and availability SLOs by workload class, how error budget is calculated and monitored, progressive canary gates, automated degradation actions (fallbacks, sampling, feature-throttle), and deterministic rollback criteria. Scope excludes Dedicated-only configuration and private on-prem policies (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
1) SLO matrix documented for 'interactive' and 'long-context' chat workloads with numeric latency and availability targets.
2) Error-budget computation defined (monthly rolling window) and dashboard widgets created showing burn, remaining budget, and per-region breakdown.
3) Rollout gates and automated actions (canary sizes, time windows, burn-rate thresholds) defined and signed off by Eng and SRE.
4) Runbook entries added for three degradation bands (informational, mitigations required, immediate rollback) with owners and Slack pager links.
5) A synthetic probe plan and alert rules created (SLO violations, burn-rate/fast-burn alarms).
6) Documented fallback model variants and config keys for automatic switching when thresholds are crossed.
7) QA: a simulated regression test demonstrating gate behavior under controlled burn (test script and results attached).
slo_matrix_summary: Workload classes: interactive (expected interactive UX), batch/long-context. Interactive: P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 350ms, P99 <= 800ms for payloads < 256 input tokens; Availability target 99.9% monthly. Long-context: P50 <= 450ms, P95 <= 1200ms, P99 <= 2000ms for payloads up to 2048 tokens; Availability target 99.5% monthly. Errors: API-level 5xx error rate <= 0.1% monthly for interactive, <= 0.25% for long-context.
error_budget_policy: Error budget window: rolling 30 days. Budget = 1 - availability_target. Example interactive target 99.9% -> monthly budget ~43.2 minutes of downtime. Burn tracking: calculate burn-rate as (observed_bad_time / allowed_bad_time) over rolling 1h, 6h, 24h windows. Gate thresholds: WARN when burn_rate >= 1.5x for 1h, PAUSE rollout when burn_rate >= 2.0x sustained for 30m, ROLLBACK when burn_rate >= 4.0x for 30m. Manual override allowed with documented approvals and post-mortem required.
degradation_bands_and_actions: Band A (informational): minor latency tail increases or small token-cost regressions. Action: notify PM/Eng, enable low-impact optimizations (adjust batch size suggestions). Band B (mitigation required): P95 or availability exceeded; action: reduce new canary traffic, enable prefix/KV cache aggressively, temporarily route to higher-capacity pools. Band C (immediate rollback): sustained error-budget burn exceeding rollback threshold; action: automatic rollback to previous model variant, revert routing rules, page SRE on-call. Each band includes exact metric thresholds and owners in the runbook.
rollout_gates: Proposed progressive rollout: Canary 1 (1% traffic, 2h), Canary 2 (10% traffic, 4h), Ramp (50% traffic, 24h), Full (100% after 72h and stable). Gate checks: per-step SLO pass for p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate below target, latency tail not regressing >10% vs baseline, and error budget burn within allowed range. Failure modes: if any gate fails, automatically pause and roll back according to error_budget_policy. Manual promotion allowed after post-check signoff by release owner and SRE.
observability_requirements: Dashboards: overall SLO summary, per-region SLOs, rollout cohort metrics, error-budget burn graphs, synthetic probe results, and per-model variant traces. Alerts: SLO breach alert (page), burn-rate threshold alerts (page escalation), canary-failure Slack channel notifications. Instrumentation: ensure request and token-level latency, queue time, model variant, batch size, region, and trace IDs are captured and exposed.
fallback_and_compatibility: Fallback policy: when Band B triggers, route new requests to a 'stable' fallback model variant (lower-latency / higher-cost) while preserving correctness. Configuration keys: fallback.enabled, fallback.max_traffic_pct, fallback.time_to_revert. Compatibility: fallback must be compatible with function-calling and structured output — a compatibility test suite will be run during canary.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decisions so far: tight p95 targets prioritized for interactive UX at cost of higher infra spend; selected rolling 30-day window to align with customer SLAs; chose multi-window burn-rate checks to detect fast regressions. Tradeoffs: aggressive rollback thresholds reduce customer exposure but increase false positives for noisy metrics. We will iterate thresholds after initial 2-month observation period.
